item.title: Broncos vs. Steelers live updates, inactives, where to watch: Pittsburgh starts Mason Rudolph following release of Aaron Rodgers, accusations against Mike McCarthy
item.description: It's been a roller coaster of a week in Pittsburgh.
item.content:encoded:
The Denver Broncos and Pittsburgh Steelers will take the field this afternoon for a special post-Thanksgiving, Black Friday matchup, with kickoff set for 3 p.m. ET at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh, airing on Amazon Prime Video. And this matchup is bound to deliver plenty of fireworks — even if not for the actual football being played on the field.

It was a week full of drama for the Steelers, as the team was sent reeling following a Week 11 upset by the Philadelphia Eagles, leading to the benching of future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup Mason Rudolph. The drama didn't end there, as Rodgers went scorched earth on Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy in an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" Wednesday after his benching, leveling a series of accusations toward his now-former coach, eventually leading to his release.

The Steelers sit at 6-4 and would be the No. 7 seed in the AFC playoffs if the season were to end today. So now, they must move forward with Rudolph as McCarthy attempts to wrangle in the chaos released in the locker room after this week's events in an attempt to maintain that playoff positioning.

The Broncos, meanwhile, sit at 8-2 in first place in the AFC West, all but locked into a playoff spot, and now with some cushion after the Kansas City Chiefs fell to the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving. After a slow start to the season, the offense has made some improvements since head coach Sean Payton resumed play calling, scoring 26-plus points in each of their past four matchups.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Broncos and Steelers face off in a special Black Friday showdown in Week 12.

item.title: Steelers fans spare no one amid Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy feud
item.description: The future Hall of Fame quarterback was released ahead of the Black Friday matchup at Acrisure Stadium after clashing with his coach over play calling.
item.content:encoded:
PITTSBURGH – Steelers fans expressed broad disgust with the state of the franchise in the hours before their team's Black Friday matchup with the Denver Broncos on Nov. 27 at Acrisure Stadium.

Aaron Rodgers’ decision to air out his grievances with the coaching in an explosive interview on ESPN’s “Pat McAfee Show” on Wednesday, Nov. 25 didn’t sit well with many.

That didn’t mean they were taking the side of coach Mike McCarthy either, though. Most seemed to believe Rodgers’ assertions that the first-year coach was falling asleep in meetings, missing them entirely and failing to conduct basic film study.

Required reading: Aaron Rodgers goes scorched earth on Mike McCarthy after Steelers benching

“It’s wild, man,” Mark Hirschfeld said as fans gathered outside Acrisure Stadium ahead of the game. “I’ve just been trying to stay awake, unlike Mike McCarthy.

“People are mad, and I don’t think they’re mad only at Aaron Rodgers, I think they’re mad at the organization as a whole. People don’t like that the Steelers are a laughingstock.”

The weather wasn’t helping the mood. It was a raw, gray and soggy November morning in the North Shore parking lots, which were filling lazily on the morning after the Thanksgiving holiday.

Tailgates were sparse beyond some hardcore zones. And many fans were reluctant to talk to USA TODAY about the state of the Steelers franchise.

Call it a citywide hangover from 48-or-so hours of chaos that began late Tuesday, when the Steelers announced they were benching Rodgers, making him inactive and starting longtime backup Mason Rudolph for a crucial game against the 8-2 Broncos.

Rodgers responded by appearing with McAfee to rhetorically torch the organization, asserting that general manager Omar Khan and owner Art Rooney II were aware of McCarthy’s alleged shortcomings and chose not to act on them by granting his preferred changes to the play calling structure. For those reasons, few were feeling sympathetic toward the front office.

“When you sign a guy like Aaron Rodgers, you are signing up for this show,” Hirschfeld said. “I don’t think anybody thought it would end any other way besides wild success or some short of giant show like this.”

'There's a reason why we're failing,' Steelers fan says

Apparently, Rooney did. He told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette on Thursday that, because of his positive experience with Rodgers in 2025, he wasn’t expecting things to go off the proverbial rails in the way they did.

Rodgers led the team to a division title a year ago. He did not play well in a playoff loss to Houston in January, but there was belief that he was the right quarterback to start the McCarthy era after he was hired to replace Mike Tomlin, because of their more than a decade of previous success together with the Green Bay Packers.

Matt Spielvogle’s feelings were mixed about who was most in the wrong.

“Whenever you have a head coach actually doing this, if it’s all true, the public deserves to know,” the Altoona, Pa., native said. “We’re paying $500 a ticket, I think the fans deserve to know what’s going on inside the locker room.

“I agree with a lot of things that [Rodgers] is doing, but I also disagree with a lot of things that he’s doing. I understand the whole secrecy. You can’t take it outside. I played college football. I get it. But at the same time, how long is it going to go on? There’s a reason why we’re failing.”

The awkward reality is that the Steelers haven't failed yet. Pittsburgh entered Week 12 at 6-4 and was the seventh seed in the AFC playoff race without a ton of pressure coming from other teams behind them.

The two-game losing streak that prompted the furor with Rodgers followed a four-game winning streak that had fans dreaming of the franchise’s first playoff win since 2016.

The offense had shown gradual improvement and defensive coordinator Patrick Graham’s soft zone coverage scheme had helped the highly-paid defense led by Cam Heyward and T.J. Watt regain some footing compared to last season.

Steelers fan resigned to future with Mike McCarthy

NFL discourse tends to exist in the present tense, though. When asked whether McCarthy should remain in place as coach beyond this season, most fans demurred or expressed a desire for the franchise to move on.

“Personally, I think let him finish out the year, then fire him,” fan Santino Fischio said just outside the North Shore’s Kamin Science Center, adjacent to Acrisure Stadium. “But do I think we’re going to do that? No.”

In fact, Rooney told the Post-Gazette that he has “100% confidence” in the coach, despite Rodgers’ assertions that he had largely lost the locker room with his conduct.

“I figured that’s how they were going to do it,” Fischio said. “I feel like they were kind of using [Rodgers] like a scapegoat.”

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Steelers fans spare no one amid Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy feud

item.title: Week 12 NFL Survivor strategy and picks
item.description: David Fucillo provides NFL Survivor pool tips in Week 12, offering up safe, value, and trap picks.
item.content:encoded:
Happy Thanksgiving! Even if you don’t celebrate the holiday, you know that it means a Thursday tripleheader of NFL action. The NFL has added a Black Friday game in recent years and now we also get a Wednesday game because the NFL clearly needs more revenue.

Last week was a relatively quiet one, with few competitive matchups and the best game of the week, Vikings vs. 49ers in Mexico City, ending up a lopsided Niners win. The hope is this week brings something a little better, and the matchups on tap suggest it should.

The week opens on Wednesday with two 6-4 squads as the Rams host the Packers. Thanksgiving brings us a huge NFC matchup between the Bears and Lions and a huge AFC matchup between the Chiefs and Bills. Black Friday features Broncos-Steelers with AFC seeding implications. Sunday brings Seahawks-49ers, and we close things out with the NFC South on Monday featuring Panthers vs. Buccaneers in Tampa.

I’m back with my Week 12 Survivor picks on Wednesday ahead of Packers-Rams. Survivor involves picking one team each week to win. If they win you advance, if they lose you’re out in most cases. I’m in one pool with four entries, but it’s also a double-elimination pool. I’m down to one entry that has one strike against it, but I’m hanging around for now.

Below I’ve got a look at the safest choices, best value picks, and then trap picks. I’ll post my own picks at the end. I’ll update on Sunday once I lock in my three picks for the weekend.

I’ve included odds for the favorite in each game, courtesy of FanDuel.

Safest picks

Jaguars (-14.5) over Titans
Bengals (-9.5) over Saints

The Jaguars are the biggest favorite this week, and it’s not close. The Bengals are the second biggest favorites and with the Saints struggling, they should roll.

Best value picks

Cowboys (-8.5) over Eagles
Jaguars (-14.5) over Titans
Commanders (-7) over Cardinals

Cowboys over Eagles is very much a trap game (see below), but at this stage of the season, there’s value in them if you wanna get a little nuts. The only game you might use them is Week 17 at home against the Giants, but that would be arguably a wilder pick given the Giants performances this season. Avoid this pick if you can, but there’s some value if you are in a pickle.

The Jaguars offer some value late in the season, traveling to face a bad Colts team in Week 18, but that’s a long ways off. First, you might not even make it to Week 18. Second, who knows what the Jaguars will or won’t have to play for and if they’ll even be playing starters. If you have them available, now is the week.

UPDATE: I forgot about the Commanders game in Arizona. You’re probably not using Washington again this season and this is a good week if you want to save the Jaguars.

Trap pick

Cowboys (-8.5) over Eagles

While there is some value, this is a tricky one given the divisional nature, the Eagles coming off a spicy win over the Steelers, and it being Thanksgiving. And the Cowboys remain a questionable option most weeks.

My picks this week

I’m rolling with the Jaguars.

UPDATE: Scratch that, I’m going with the Commanders. I want to save the Jaguars for December, so we’ll roll the dice with Washington. It’s a road game, but Arizona stinks.

item.title: Lions fan chokes out Bears supporter in vicious Thanksgiving brawl
item.description: The Chicago Bears got the better of the Detroit Lions when the two teams faced off on Thanksgiving Day, winning a thriller, 39-35. But a Lions fan got the best...
item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Bears got the better of the Detroit Lions when the two teams faced off on Thanksgiving Day, winning a thriller, 39-35.

But a Lions fan got the best of a Bears supporter in a wild brawl that took place inside Detroit’s Ford Field while the game was underway.

The video was initially posted on Instagram by Metro Detroit News and started with a Lions fan raining punches down on the Bears fan, who he is already on top of despite numerous people nearby trying to pull him off.

After several punches, the Lions fan wraps his arm around the Bears fan’s neck and seemingly tried to choke him out.

The two men fell to the ground a few seconds later but seemed to be in the same position.

Then another fan wearing a black jacket appears to try and stomp on one of the fans before getting pulled away, at which point the video ended.

It’s unclear what sparked the fight between these two fans.

But the Lions and the Bears are bitter rivals, and this is surely not the first time fans of the two teams have resorted to blows.

Brawls between fans at NFL games have been a recurring theme over the past several weeks, with multiple videos of these ugly scraps going viral every weekend.

Apparently even on a day of thanks, Thanksgiving, some fans are unable to hold their emotions in check. A wild video surfaced late Thursday of an Eagles fan manhandling two Cowboys fans in a fracas.

That came on the heels of Rams and Packers supporters going toe-to-toe on Wednesday night.

item.title: Seahawks fan chat: Broncos take on DK Metcalf’s Steelers on Black Friday
item.description: Will Metcalf get ejected again? Will Mason Rudolph be better than Aaron Rodgers? Let’s watch Broncos-Steelers together, Seahawks fans!
item.content:encoded:
The Seattle Seahawks have four losses on the season, and three of them are to teams with combined records of 26-5. One of those teams is the Denver Broncos, whom at 9-2 are in the driver’s seat to win the AFC West again. In this Black Friday special, the Broncos will be facing the Pittsburgh Steelers, who have had a totally normal week.

Aaron Rodgers entered Monday as Pittsburgh’s starting quarterback, while there was speculation over DK Metcalf possibly getting suspended for the Broncos game following his Week 11 ejection. Well, Metcalf didn’t get suspended, and then he had an all-timer of a fade into the backdrop after the Steelers benched and subsequently waived Rodgers. To the surprise of no one, Rodgers went in full attack mode on McCarthy, airing out behind-the-scenes stuff that usually never sees the light of day. I guess the 1-2-3 Packers gaffed by McCarthy was real, though.

Anyway, the Steelers are 6-4 after starting out 6-2, and Mason Rudolph is tasked with saving what is a rapidly spiraling season. This game is intriguing for totally different reasons than first imagined.

The Browns will be on Sunday Night Football this weekend, but it remains to be seen if rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston will be in their lineup.

Boston missed his third straight practice on Friday with a quad injury and the team listed him as questionable to face the Raiders. The second-round pick has not missed a game this season and has 33 catches for 523 yards and three touchdowns in 10 contests.

Defensive end Derek Barnett (hamstring) also missed practice all week and has been ruled out for this Sunday.

item.title: Chicago Bears Injury Updates on Colston Loveland and Dayo Odeyingbo
item.description: We have good news/bad news on the Chicago Bears injury front today. @wiltfongjr has the details here.
item.content:encoded:
In the first quarter of yesterday’s game in Detroit, Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland was injured when he was rolled up from behind. The Bears called it a knee injury, and he was carted off the field, frustrated and in tears. Today’s news is much more optimistic, as ESPN’s Courtnet Cronin wrote, “Per league source, Bears tight end Colston Loveland is considered week-to-week with the left knee injury. He will get a second opinion soon, but no determination on whether he is an IR candidate has been made.”

Cronin’s report came about a half hour after ESPN’s Adam Schefter also shared positive news about Loveland: “There still is additional testing to be done, but the current belief is that Loveland could return later this season.”

Schefter’s initial report also included that an injured reserve stint was expected, which would mean Loveland would be out a minimum of four games, but he followed up with a report that corroborated Cornin’s: “Until Colston Loveland gets a second opinion on his knee injury, the Bears are not making any decisions about injured reserve, and he will be considered a week-to-week until then.”

There are six games remaining in the regular season, so in the best-case scenario, we will see Colston again.

In the meantime, the Bears have two active tight ends on the 53-man roster, Sam Roush and Stephen Carlson, and they have 26-year-old Qadir Ismail (6’6″, 232) on the practice squad.

Earlier today, the Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs reported that defensive lineman Dayo Odeyingbo underwent surgery and won’t return this season.

Odeyingbo injured his quad in Week 5 and was in the midst of a solid 2026, with 9 tackles, 3 tackles for loss, 3 sacks, and 2 passes defended while playing up and down Chicago’s defensive line.

For those curious, Dayo has one more year left on his contract, and his 2027 cap hit would be $26,500,000. If cut, there would be $11,500,000 in dead money.

item.title: Johnson will start again for the Cardinals against Washington
item.description: Musical chairs in the QB room this year
item.content:encoded:
Every week for the Arizona Cardinals, there is quarterback news. Good or bad, this group has something going on that needs to be mentioned.

Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur has decided to start QB Josh Johnson against the Washington Commanders Sunday in the late game.

RELATED: CARDINALS FANS WANT LAFLEUR TO STAY

Rookie QB Carson Beck has been ruled out due to continued back issues.

Johnson got the start last weekend against the Kansas City Chiefs, a 34-7 loss on the road. Johnson went 18 for 31 for 155 yards with one TD toss against zero picks. He was sacked three times and had an 82.1 QB rating.

On the Cardinals second drive of the game, Johnson orchestrated a 10-play drive that began at their own 37-yard line and gained 63-yards. The drive had six passing plays, one sack, and three runs that gained just five yards. A 25-yard pass and run by WR Harrison Wallace was the highlight. On a first and goal from the Chiefs’ two, Johnson found WR Simi Fehoko crossing deep in the end zone for the touchdown.

At that point, the score was 14-7. That pretty much was the highlight of the game for Arizona’s offense.

So for now, Johnson will get his second start after signing with the team on November 10. With one day of practice, he started under center for the Cardinals.

Arizona claimed rookie QB Joey Aguilar off the practice squad of the Jacksonville Jaguars, who is currently listed as Johnson’s backup. This week, the Cardinals claimed former signalcaller Kedon Slovis off waivers from the Baltimore Ravens. He is listed as QB3. It is possible that Aguilar and Slovis could be flipped as Slovis already knows this new Arizona offense.

LaFleur mentioned that Beck could be ready to play in Week 13 at home against the Philadelphia Eagles.

LaFleur also stated that OG Jon Gaines is also ruled out against the Commanders.

item.title: Packers Film Room: Love tosses a TD to Watson
item.description: The Green Bay Packers scored a touchdown this week, so let’s talk about it
item.content:encoded:
It was not a pretty game and there’s plenty of time for all of that before the next game. But we also got a Love-to-Watson TD this week, so I wanted to spend a little time with that.

The Green Bay Packers are in 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR) in a 3×1 bunch look. The bunch consists of Christian Watson [9] at the point, Matthew Golden [0] on the outside and Tucker Kraft [85] on the inside. Savion Williams [83] is split wide to the right.

Before the snap, Kraft goes in a return motion, trying to get a tell from the defense. No one follows Kraft as he motions to the inside, but the Rams do start to rotate their safeties. The man over Kraft starts to rotate to the middle while the middle safety starts down to the line where it looks like Kraft is motioning. When Kraft returns to the bunch, the Rams shift back to their original positions. No one follows Kraft across the formation, but that rotation looks like a Man coverage rotation.

On the right side of the field, the Packers are running a Slant/Rail combo with Williams and Kaleb Johnson [26]. On the left, Watson takes off on a drag route while Kraft and Golden are running a version of Pile (Pile Swirl?), with Kraft running an out-cutting route to the pylon while Golden runs a swirl route underneath.

Love checks Jaylen McCollough [2] in the middle to see what he is doing. McCullough drops back into a middle zone, reading Love. Watson comes streaking into Love’s vision and Love is able to confirm Man coverage: Watson on Josh Wallace [30]. Watson is a burner and Wallace is on the slower side for a cornerback (he ran a 4.68 40 at his Pro Day), so that’s a pretty big disparity. Watson running a drag route in Man coverage means he is able to gain separation as he runs across the field, running away from his man coverage assignment. And if that man runs a 4.68 40, so much the better.

With the right side cleared out (the Slant draws the defender inside and the Rail draws the defender deep), there is no help coming.

Love hits his back foot, bounces, then loads and fires to Watson.

item.title: Cleveland Browns vs. Raiders: One matchup that could be key to a win
item.description: RT Tytus Howard will be in the spotlight against DE Maxx Crosby. Who wins that matchup could unlock a Victory Monday.
item.content:encoded:
The Cleveland Browns have been a bit of an adventure on offense through the first 10 games of the season.

Bumble around for three quarters, make plays when they need to in the fourth quarter, and pull out a last-minute win. It’s a script that, while exciting, is also not one that feels sustainable on a week-to-week basis.

Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders appears to be a prime opportunity for the Browns to get something going on offense, as the Raiders defense is:

  • 30th in total defense
  • 31st in run defense
  • 26th in pass defense
  • 32nd in points allowed
  • 30th in RZ TDs allowed
  • 29th in third-down stops

But if Cleveland is going to get its offense untracked for a full season, they will need to contend with defensive end Maxx Crosby, who needs just a half-sack to hit 75 career sacks. And with Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson having taken 37 sacks, the second-most in the league coming into Week 12, Crosby could be in line for a big day.

Crosby’s ability to disrupt an offense was on offensive coordinator Travis Switzer’s mind during his weekly media appearance:

“I think Crosby is probably as disruptive of a player as there is on defense in this league. And really, this is not a knock; this is a credit to him. It starts with his relentless effort. Not that he’s not talented; he’s very talented, and he’s long, but I’ve always respected him. I think he plays the game the right way. He only knows one speed, and he’s going full speed at all times.

“I think it’s an every-down disruption. Like some guys, they seem to show up maybe a little bit more on pass downs. I mean, he’s making plays on every down, whether it’s run or pass; he’s knifing the C-gap. He’s a guy that you just have to be aware of on every down, not just passing situations. And like I said, it starts with his physical ability, his length, his quickness, but also just his relentless play style.”

One of the players who will be tasked with slowing down Crosby is right tackle Tytus Howard, as Pro Football Focus highlighted the matchup as one of the 10 best to watch this weekend:

A revamped Sunday night showdown gives rookie Fernando Mendoza another big opportunity against the Browns under the lights. In this matchup between playoff hopefuls, Crosby vs. Howard will be defining.

Crosby hasn’t been affected by a bad overall season by Las Vegas’ defense. His 86.1 overall PFF grade is the fifth-highest among qualified edge defenders, including tying for fifth at the position with 50 pressures.

Howard has helped revitalize Cleveland’s offensive line since arriving from Houston. Although he’s surrendered 21 pressures, only two have been converted into sacks. That’s lifted him to a 77.9 PFF pass-blocking grade, tying for 16th among qualified tackles this season.

Howard hasn’t let up a sack in 248 snaps, with his last coming in Week 4. Crosby, who was slowed by Mike McGlinchey and help against the Broncos in Week 11, will look to end that in another hostile road atmosphere.

The NFL gave the Browns a primetime stage on Sunday night to showcase to the nation that they are serious about staying in the AFC playoff race.

Keeping Crosby in check and out of the backfield will be a major step toward achieving that goal.

item.title: Jaguars star receiver Parker Washington to miss Week 12 in troublesome injury concern
item.description: Jacksonville's star receiver is "week to week" and will miss Sunday's game against the Titans with a shoulder injury suffered in practice Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
The Jaguars have seven weeks to let Parker Washington heal.

Jacksonville’s star receiver is “week to week” and will miss Sunday’s game against the Titans with a shoulder injury suffered in practice Thursday.

“Hope to have him back ASAP,” Jaguars coach Liam Coen said, “but week-to-week injury.”

The week-to-week indication means there is some concern about a multi-week absence, although it’s seemingly a positive sign that Coen didn’t indicate this could be a season-ending blow.

The Jaguars (7-3) are in the fortunate spot where they have a clear path to winning the AFC South and can afford being down a top player.

They own a three-game lead over the Texans, although Houston beat them earlier this season, and the teams meet in Houston in Week 15.

Jacksonville sits as the AFC’s No. 3 seed due to its head-to-head win over the Bengals, and is one game behind the Broncos, whom they lost to in Week 2.

Washington, 24, is enjoying a breakout season and is on pace to set new career highs in targets and receiving yards after already setting his new mark for touchdowns.

The fourth-year receiver leads the team with his 44 catches, 81 targets, 748 receiving yards and six receiving touchdowns, emerging as Trevor Lawrence’s go-to target.

Last week in the loss to the Giants, he had what would have been an incredible touchdown overturned in a polarizing decision.

The injury comes at an unfortunate personal time since he’s in a contract year and does not have a new deal in place with the Jaguars.

Veteran Jakobi Meyers now projects as Lawrence’s top target, although there are now more opportunities available for veteran Brian Thomas Jr. and rookie Josh Cameron.

“Just tweaks a couple things,” Coen said. “Formational, obviously guys have to step up, feel very confident in the guy in the group that we have … everybody has to step up a little bit.’

Jacksonville’s first test without Washington comes against a Titans team it beat 40-23 two weeks ago, but a tough road clash looms in Week 13 against the NFC North-leading Bears.

item.title: Bears stuck in injury purgatory as Colston Loveland awaits second opinion
item.description: The Bears will have to turn to the next man up -- again.
item.content:encoded:
The Bears will have to turn to the next man up — again.

Chicago lost tight end Colston Loveland in the first quarter of its thrilling 39-35 win over the Lions on Thanksgiving, and it appears he’ll be sidelined for a while.

Loveland, 22, is dealing with a knee sprain and is considered week-to-week as he awaits a second opinion, according to ESPN.

The team will reportedly wait to make a decision regarding injured reserve, which would take him out of action for four weeks, at minimum.

There is optimism he’ll be back before the season is over and be back for the playoffs — with the NFC East-leading Bears (9-2) having a 95% probability of making the postseason.

He’s become a reliable target for quarterback Caleb Williams, hauling in 40 catches for 393 yards and three touchdowns on the season.

Loveland’s injury further stresses a thinned-out tight end room in Chicago, which already lost Cole Kmet to a season-ending knee injury in Week 7.

That leaves bigger duties to rookie Sam Roush and Stephen Carlson, who saw his first NFL game action in six seasons after getting called up from the practice squad earlier this month.

Roush caught all five of his career-high five targets for 31 yards, while Carlson had two first-down catches on Chicago’s first scoring drive.

“They did a phenomenal job,” Johnson said. “Seeing them just continue to get better and better and better, [Roush] had a little hiccups there earlier in the season, and now he’s really smoothed out and he’s only going to continue to ascend. I mean, I’ve got a lot of confidence in him as a blocker. We saw him — we threw to him, I think he had five catches this game, and so he’s become the security blanket there for our quarterback as well. We’ll see if he needs to have a bigger role here going forward.

“And then Carlson, I mean, when I first came to the building a year and a half ago, [tight ends coach] Jimmy Dray, he just pounded the table like, ‘You’re going to love this guy. He’s dependable, he does everything right, and we’re going to use him at some point.’ And here we go, in one of the biggest games that we’ve had in a year and a half, and he doesn’t miss a beat. So, it’s who he is, and we’re very fortunate to have him.”

The Bears will have some time to figure things out with the next game slated for Dec. 6 at home against the Jaguars — who are dealing with their own injury issues with receiver Parker Washington also considered week-to-week after suffering a shoulder injury during Thursday’s practice.

item.title: Brian Schottenheimer on failed fourth-down try: "I trust our quarterback and our offense"
item.description: The Eagles' path to erasing a 31-10 third-quarter deficit included many favorable twists and turns.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles' path to erasing a 31-10 third-quarter deficit included many favorable twists and turns. The last one was a gift from the Cowboys.

With 55 seconds left — and with the Eagles having no timeouts — the Cowboys faced fourth and one from the Philadelphia 39. After attempting to get the Eagles to jump offside, the Cowboys took a timeout and decided to go for it.

The Cowboys lined up in shotgun formation. Quarterback Dak Prescott looked to the right, presumably to connect on a slant to receiver CeeDee Lamb. Lamb was jammed hard by cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. Prescott waited for Lamb to get free. When Prescott decided to pursue another option, he was sacked.

The play lost nine yards, giving the Eagles the ball at their own 48.

Why not punt? Why not force quarterback Joe Milton III to drive into field-goal range, with less than 50 seconds to play and no timeouts?

Coach Brian Schottenheimer was asked about the decision after the game.

"Really felt good about the drive we had going, and felt really good that we were gonna put the game away there," Schottenheimer told reporters. "And I wanted the ball in Dak's hands. And, unfortunately, we weren't able to make it work."

Does Schottenheimer ever second-guess himself?

"All the time," he said. "Not in that situation. Absolutely not in that situation."

Why not?

"I trust our quarterback and our offense," Schottenheimer said.

That's fine. But it's not about "trust." It's about whether it makes sense to assume the offense will execute in that moment, and what the consequence will be if the defense executes a little better.

It's about making an assessment, based on years of watching, playing, and coaching football, as to whether the risk of not converting outweighed the risk of the Eagles driving from their own 20 (or perhaps deep inside their own 20) into field goal range.

Maybe the truth is that Schottenheimer didn't trust his defense to keep that from happening. Regardless, his "trust" in the offense was ultimately misplaced. And the Cowboys lost another game when they scored 30 or more points.

item.title: Dolphins cornerback JuJu Brents to miss Sunday’s game against New York Jets
item.description: Brents will sit with shoulder and knee injuries.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Dolphins continued their preparation today for Sunday’s tilt against AFC East division foes, the New York Jets. Head coach Jeff Hafley met with the South Florida media this morning and gave a trio of updates regarding three Dolphins starters who are dealing with various injuries.

Hafley said that starting right tackle Austin Jackson and starting safety Dante Trader Jr. will play against New York on Sunday, but that starting cornerback JuJu Brents will miss the game due to shoulder and knee injuries.

Brents has been solid when suiting up for Miami this season, however the player has a lengthy injury history, which could make general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan’s evaluation of him a little murky this offseason. Miami’s young cornerback is on the last year of his rookie contract — as he was drafted by the Indianapolis Colts in the 2nd round (44th overall) in the 2023 NFL Draft.

Thankfully, Darrell Baker Jr. returned to action last week after a stay on the physically unable to perform list. The Dolphins will lean on the veteran in Brent’s absence, as well as rookie Chris Johnson, second-year player Jason Marshall Jr. and others.

We will continue to keep you updated on all things Miami Dolphins as the team tries for their second win this season against the New York Jets on Sunday.

item.title: Brian Schottenheimer report card: Is it finally over for the head coach?
item.description: Do you think the Cowboys will actually move on from Brian Schottenheimer?
item.content:encoded:
There was a lot of talk this week about the Dallas Cowboys attempting to make a run at the NFC East after dismantling the Tennessee Titans in week 11.

All of that talk seems silly now, given what we know about this football team. Through 28 games as the Cowboys head coach, Brian Schottenheimer’s team has won back-to-back games just twice (weeks 11-13 last season). Since then, the Cowboys have alternated wins and losses or lost consecutive games. This is now a large enough sample size to see the writing on the wall.

The Cowboys held a 31-10 lead late in the third quarter on Thanksgiving before the Cowboys abysmal defense and conservative play-calling on offense saw their lead squander with just minutes to go in the fourth quarter. After a quick three-and-out from the Cowboys defense to kickoff the second half, the Cowboys offense responded with a five-play, three-minute drive that led to a punt.

On that drive (one that could have pretty much put the game away), the Cowboys ran the ball on first down for two yards, connected on a 22-yard passing play on second down, then followed it up with a run of negative five on first down, an eight-yard run on second down, and then a Dak Prescott sack on third down.

That drive encapsulates everything that is wrong with the Schottenheimer offense. After Prescott torched the Eagles defense for the entire first half, and the officials calling defensive pass interference at a high rate, the Cowboys elected to start their run-heavy, clock-killing offensive approach that would ultimately cost them the game, and practically end their season.

After the Cowboys first drive of the second half, the Cowboys kicked a field goal on 4th-and-11 to push the score to 31-17. Their first drive in the fourth quarter was three straight runs for nine yards. Schottenheimer had his offense on the field with a 21-point lead on 4th-and-1 from the Dallas 35-yard line. Instead of going for the kill, Schottenheimer did his trademark thing of attempting to get the defense to jump offsides, before taking the delay of game and punting. One issue, the punt was blocked and returned for a touchdown to cut the lead to 31-24.

The Cowboys offense responded with a touchdown drive on a 14-yard rushing touchdown from Prescott taking the score to 38-24. The Eagles would respond with a touchdown of their own three plays later, cutting the lead back to 38-30.

Their next offensive drive started with a first down run, a holding penalty, an incompletion to Kavonte Turpin, and then an illegal forward pass penalty that called back an 84-yard touchdown. A Brandon Aubrey missed 40-yard field goal with 3:27 left in the fourth quarter put every Cowboys’ fan watching in the worst place. After yet another quick, four-play drive for a touchdown, the Cowboys offense had the football with a two-point lead with 2:10 left to close out the game.

The Cowboys started off the drive with a two-yard run to take the clock to the two-minute warning (smart!). They would come out of the two-minute warning with Prescott firing a dart into Brevyn Spann-Ford for a gain of 15 (smart!). After that play, Schottenheimer called three straight run plays that did not move the chains and elected to go for it on 4th-and-1 to ice the game.

The decision to go for it over attempting another long field goal with a kicker who has struggled mightily this season was the correct one, but the play call could not have been worse. Needing just one yard to get to 6-6 on the season, Schottenheimer had Prescott come out in shotgun with no play-action running George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb on slants, with all other targets running hitches. No one was anywhere near open and with the Eagles bringing a blitz, Prescott was sacked for a loss of nine. The Eagles last-second field goal after that ended the game, and the season, for the Dallas Cowboys.

Needing just one yard on fourth down, lining up in the gun and the non-use of play-action is just inexcusable for a play-caller who has been doing this for over two decades. No motion, no threat of a run, and no creativity in the design on the Cowboys biggest play of the game was as disappointing as possible.

Schottenheimer called a good game in the first half, but he did so by being aggressive and allowing Prescott to run the offense through the passing game. In the second half, we saw a similar game script to the Arizona Cardinals game, where they attempted to bleed clock and settled for field goals and trusting the defense.

What do you know? The end result was exactly the same. After so many embarrassing performances this year from the Cowboys, it’s just hard to even imagine a scenario in which Brian Schottenheimer could return next year. The fanbase lost a ton of interest towards the end of the Mike McCarthy experience, but this offseason would likely surpass that by flying colors if Jerry Jones announced Schottenheimer will return as head coach and/or play-caller in 2027.

Play-Calling

C-

This was truly a tale of two halves for Schottenheimer the play-caller. It was a very good first half, but like he has done far too often this season, his conservative nature and faith in his defense ended up costing the Cowboys another win. Overall, he gets a C- due to the major fall off in the second-half and the disastrous 4th-and-1 play call on the biggest play of the game.

Fourth-Down Decisions

C-

Similar to play calling, he made the correct decision to go for it on every fourth down that they did, but his decision to punt on the blocked punt was a major whiff in my opinion.

Timeout Usage

F

Like we have seen so often this season, Schottenheimer’s use of timeouts in this game made no sense.

Team Preparation

D

Again, a tale of two halves. The team looked great in the first half, but completely fell apart in the second half. For a coach who talks so much about consistency and playing all three phases in all four quarters, the Cowboys have been really poor at doing just that in Schottenheimer’s time as head coach.

What grade would you give to Brian Schottenheimer on Sunday?

item.title: Pick-Six: New York Jets at Miami Dolphins
item.description: Can the Jets avoid a Dolphins sweep?
item.content:encoded:
Having returned to winning ways on Sunday, the Jets will be facing another struggling opponent this weekend as they travel to Miami to face the 1-9 Dolphins. New York will be looking to atone for their 28-25 loss to the Dolphins last month.

Here are six storylines to watch as New York look to start stacking wins:

A perfect full circle moment

The Jets haven’t actually won in Miami since 2014, at which time their quarterback was a certain Geno Smith. This ended up being one of a signature games of Smith’s career, as he posted a perfect quarterback rating and led New York to a 37-24 win.

Smith makes his return to Miami as the Jets quarterback trying to end that 12 year wait for a Jets’ win over their AFC East rivals on their own turf and he’ll head there with the Jets as a 3.5-point road favorite.

Will David Onyemata’s return make any difference?

The Jets made a couple of moves on the defensive line on Tuesday, which is a surefire sign that David Onyemata is about to return having been activated from injured reserve to practice all last week.

For New York, the run defense has been one of their main weaknesses since early in the season and Onyemata should elevate them in this area. Ollie Gordon II rushed for over 100 yards and helped Miami run out the clock in the first meeting between these teams so the Jets must improve in this area.

With nose tackle T’Vondre Sweat also out, rookie Darrell Jackson Jr. has also started to flash and he could take his game to another level with a more experienced disruptor next to him. (Note: The Jets also activated Sweat for practice on Wednesday).

Is Sterling Shepard going to stick around?

With Omar Cooper and Isaiah Williams both out, the Jets opted to elevate Sterling Shepard from the practice squad and he came up big with two touchdown catches in Sunday’s win. After making these plays in the red zone – another area where the Jets had been floundering – could the Jets really consider taking him back out of the line-up?

The issue is that Shepard has been elevated three times from the practice squad already so he will need to be signed to the active roster if he’s to keep playing. They could potentially opt to have Shepard and Tim Patrick swap places, so that Patrick can be elevated himself three times from the practice squad if necessary. Another alternative would be to send Malik McClain back down and perhaps use Kene Nwangwu as a replacement punt gunner for the time being.

If Cooper and Williams are both still out, it seems certain the Jets will find a way to get Shepard in the line-up but if one or both is ready to return, the situation is less clear.

Is Kenyon Sadiq about to break out?

With each of our first three storylines to watch being about players in their thirties, you begin to wonder where the priorities lie in terms of developing their young players and getting them involved more.

One such player is Kenyon Sadiq, who failed to build on his big breakout game in Detroit but is starting to show some positive signs over the past few weeks. He had three catches for 30 yards against the Chargers and four for 49 against the Chiefs three weeks ago. Other than that Lions game, these represent his best passing game outputs of the season.

Sadiq has arguably been more impactful than advertised as a blocker and has proven to be a versatile weapon even though he hasn’t been used much. This might be a good week to ramp up his usage and see how he responds with the bye week upcoming.

Will Kyle McCord be any better than last week?

The main difference for the Dolphins in terms of the team that beat the Jets last month and the current team is that they are now without quarterback Malik Willis.

In his place, Kyle McCord – having previously never thrown an NFL pass – has not been impressive. He passed for 209 yards in a close loss to the Colts, but then completed just 12 of 33 passes for 102 yards in Sunday’s 26-9 loss to the Bills.

McCord has been sacked five times with one fumble and one interception in his two starts so far.

Redemption time for Minkah Fitzpatrick?

Former Dolphins safety Minkah Fitzpatrick hasn’t made a big impact with the Jets yet, although it was him who ended their long interception drought against the Bears.

In the previous meeting against Miami, it was Fitzpatrick’s missed tackle on Caleb Douglas that led to a long touchdown to ultimately clinch the win for the Dolphins. He’ll therefore be doubly motivated to lead New York to the win this time.

Let us know how you see things going in Sunday’s game in the comments section…

item.title: The Seahawks have one weakness that the 49ers can exploit
item.description: We go over 3 numbers to know ahead of the 49ers-Seahawks matchup
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco 49ers look to continue their quest for perfection in the NFC West with their home tilt against the Seattle Seahawks.

The two met in October in a turnover-heavy game that ended 32-29 in Seattle.

While both teams are dealing with ailing quarterbacks, it looks like Sam Darnold is on track to play on Sunday, while as of Thursday night, Brock Purdy’s status is unclear. While Mac Jones started eight games in 2025, none came against the Seahawks, and that defense is a tough draw for any backup quarterback.

But as we wait to know if Purdy is good to go, these are the numbers to know for Sunday’s NFC West clash: 

26.8

Pressure rate. The Seahawks offense has allowed a 26.8 pressure rate, the third-highest rate in the league (according to Pro Football Reference). 

The 49ers defensive line has been turning up the heat on opposing quarterbacks over the past few weeks, a welcome sight for a group that struggled for most of the first half of the season. After combining for 15 pressures against Atlanta and Las Vegas, the San Francisco front had 26 pressures against Dallas and 21 against Minnesota last week.

And while those 47 pressures only translated to two sacks, Seattle doesn’t allow too much of that pressure to get to Sam Darnold. Seattle has allowed only 22 sacks this season (12th-fewest) and a 6.7 sack rate (14th-best); however, pressure might be enough against Darnold, who appears on track to play Sunday. 

When under pressure (according to Pro Football Focus), Darnold completes 37.2 percent of his passes with a pair of touchdowns to five interceptions, good for a passer rating of 34.4, 34th of 37 qualified passers this season. 

Darnold threw a pair of interceptions in Week 5 against 23 San Francisco pressures. Maybe the 49ers front can squeeze out a bit more production on Sunday to force another multi-turnover game from the Seattle quarterback. 

4.5

Yards per pass attempt. The Seahawks defense allows 4.5 yards per pass attempt, the league’s best average.

The 49ers offense is predicated on the run game staying ahead of the sticks, and using the pass game for the explosive plays. San Francisco’s 9.0 yards per pass attempt is the top in the league, and if that pace continues, it would become the 24th offense in NFL history (1920-present day, per Pro Football Reference) to average more than nine yards per attempt.

But Seattle’s defense does not allow much in the passing game, allowing half of what the 49ers gain per pass attempt. Seattle has allowed more than 200 passing yards in only one game this season and has already held the 49ers to a season-low 175 passing yards in San Francisco’s Week 5 win.

The Seattle pass defense will be tricky enough with a healthy Brock Purdy, but a less-than-healthy or even a Mac Jones spot start might prove to be too tough for the 49ers offense. 

69.6

Red zone touchdown percentage. Seattle’s defense allows a touchdown on 69.6 percent of red zone chances, the fourth-highest rate in the league.

Another week, another tough red zone defense for the 49ers offense to handle. Last week, it was a Minnesota team where it was tough to both enter the red zone and score from inside it. San Francisco went four-for-four from the final 20 yards against the feared Vikings defense.

With Seattle, it might be tough to enter the red zone, but once in, the Seahawks are among the worst in the league at allowing red zone touchdowns. After the 49ers’ four red zone entries against the Vikings, Seattle jumped Minnesota into the top spot, tied with Pittsburgh with only 23 red zone attempts allowed this season. 

But where Seattle’s defense falls off is stopping the touchdown. While the 16 red zone touchdowns allowed is among the ten fewest in the league, 16 touchdowns on 23 entries comes out to 69.6 percent, placing the elite Seattle defense ahead of only Carolina, Washington, and Las Vegas.

The 49ers offense went three-for-three against Seattle in Week 5, adding to their first-ranked 84.8 red zone touchdown percentage entering Week 11. The Seahawks might make life hell for the 49ers in the first 80 yards, but if San Francisco can get to the final 20, you have to like their chances to come out with six points.

T.J. Hockenson (vs. ATL) - 44.5 proj. yards

Hockenson is benefiting from the Kirk Cousins trade and the Jordan Addison injury. He is the TE8 on TE6 usage over his last four games, seeing between 7.6 and 10.1 expected half PPR points in all four contests. He's a stable low-end TE1 option.

Atlanta ranks 14th in half PPR points allowed to tight ends at 10.9 points per game. The Falcons have been better against the position of late, but they're without FS Jessie Bates III now. Minnesota enters as 7-point home favorites with an implied team total of 24.25 points (eighth).

Cam Skattebo (at IND) - 95.5 proj. total yards

Skattebo dominated touches again. He had 14 carries and seven targets in an upset win against the Jaguars, leading to 17.0 expected half PPR points. Despite fumbling in the second half, the Giants stuck with him and he ultimately closed the game out with a backflip. It's almost as simple as they don't want Devin Singletary on the field anymore, which means Skattebo should float to some nice RB1/2 weeks.

The bad news is his tape last week was pretty rough, as was J.J. McCarthy's. They won't face a loaded Jaguars defense every week, but Skattebo is at risk of being benched if he continues to put the ball on the dirt. His range of outcomes remain wide, but there is clear upside if he can keep it together.

This is a matchup to feel confident in with the Colts very clearly tanking. They've allowed 26.5 half PPR points to RB rooms over their past four games, on 152 rushing YPG. David Montgomery had 124 total yards, Ollie Gordon II had 115, Javonte Williams had 124 and Bhayshul Tuten had 159. This is a blowup spot with the Giants projected for 24.0 points.

Chase Brown (vs. NO) - 73.5 proj. total yards

That was a painful primetime game from Brown, who dropped multiple targets and took six carries for just six yards. He's the RB21 on RB15 usage this season, as one of the most inefficient players with the context of how great this Bengals offense is. I'm not sure if he's even better than Samaje Perine, who is one of the most underrated insurance options as we close out the fantasy season. This offense gives Brown multi-score upside as we saw in Week 10, but those were out of structure receiving touchdowns. Perine threatens at the goal line and now in the two-minute drill. He's a volatile fantasy RB2, as he's been throughout the year. Brown is leading the position in receptions per game (5.2).

The Saints offer one of the friendliest matchups in football, ranking second in half PPR points allowed to running backs at 25.6 points per game. New Orleans ranks third in rushing points allowed (18.4 per game) and eighth in receiving points allowed to the position, having recently surrendered big games to Chuba Hubbard (RB4) and Jaylen Warren (RB17). Cincinnati features the league's highest neutral pass rate at 67% (first) and enters as 10-point home favorites with an implied total of 30.75 points (second).

Quinshon Judkins (vs. LV) - 67.5 proj. total yards

Judkins is the RB23 on RB25 usage since pass-catching backup Dylan Sampson has returned to the lineup. Judkins' receiving role has been bad over the past month (1.8 receptions per game), so he's entirely touchdown dependent as a FLEX option. The good news is his workload is pretty stable, putting up between 10.7 and 12.6 expected half PPR points in five-straight games.

The Raiders rank fourth in half PPR points allowed to running backs, yielding 24.6 points per game. That vulnerability is almost entirely on the ground, where Las Vegas ranks first in rushing points allowed to backs (19.5 per game), compared to ranking 28th against receiving backs. That's okay for Judkins!!! Jonah Coleman (RB1) and Braelon Allen (RB7) each posted top-10 finishes against them recently. Cleveland sits as 4.5-point home favorites with an implied total of 23.0 points (15th).

Jaylen Warren (vs. DEN) - 85.5 proj. total yards

Last week was a nightmare game. There weren't many lanes on film review, and he couldn't bring in what could've been a 31-yard receiving TD on a ball that was a bit high on Aaron Rodgers. Beyond that, the Steelers were trailing, which meant Warren and Rico Dowdle combined for just five touches in the second half. Across the entire season, Warren is averaging 2.6 expected half PPR points fewer in games with Dowdle at this point, on 4.0 fewer carries and 1.2 fewer targets per game. Warren is back to being a firm fantasy RB2.

The matchup is one that comes with some advantages and some weaknesses. The Broncos have a strong DL, one that will put pressure on their backup LG. Denver also has very concerning LB play, while having standouts at all corner spots. The ball typically gets funneled to RBs against the Broncos, who are allowing the ninth-most fantasy points to the position on 126 rushing yards per game (10th). Ashton Jeanty popped up for 169 total yards last week, while Chuba Hubbard (96) and Emmett Johnson (143) hit them hard in the outings before that. The Steelers only project for 17.25 points (30th), so the lack of floor is alarming.
